prompt:
Build a physically causal four-cylinder in-line diesel fuel-injection system in Simscape Fluids. A common rotating camshaft must drive one low-pressure lift pump and four separately phased positive-displacement injection-pump elements. Feed all four elements from the lift-pump circuit, connect each element through its own high-pressure delivery path to a spring-loaded needle injector, and return spill and injector discharge flow to a common reservoir. The four cylinders must inject in the firing order 1-3-4-2.

Read EngineSpeed_rad_s and FuelControl_m from the MATLAB base workspace and support their declared ranges.

EngineSpeed_rad_s is a real scalar in [80, 120] rad/s for the common camshaft, and FuelControl_m is a real scalar in [0.0015, 0.0025] m for the common fuel-metering displacement command. FuelControl_m is a common mechanical metering command for the four pumping elements: changing it must alter delivered fuel through the physical pumping and spill paths rather than rescaling recorded signals. At the nominal inputs of 100 rad/s and 0.002 m, all four injectors must generate distinct, repeatable injection pulses with comparable delivered volume. The lift pump, plungers, delivery valves, compressible fuel paths, and injector needles must causally participate in those pulses.

Log complete-interval MATLAB Timeseries named injection_delivery, pump_kinematics, and injector_state. injection_delivery has 4 channels in injector 1--4 order, each the injector volume flow in m^3/s. pump_kinematics has 8 channels: plunger 1--4 position (m), followed by plunger 1--4 velocity (m/s). injector_state has 8 channels: needle 1--4 lift (m), followed by injector 1--4 chamber pressure (Pa). All channels must come from the same physical simulation; duplicated or prescribed pulse traces are not valid substitutes for four functioning pumping and injector paths.

Save the completed model as cand_XFLUID10.slx in the submission directory and keep the latest usable state saved there throughout the task.

Submission filename contract: create, edit, and save the final self-contained Simulink model as cand_XFLUID10.slx in the assigned submission directory; keep the latest usable state at that exact path throughout the run.
